business_problem: Lenztech had to process millions of retail shelf images and massive SKU catalogs every day while maintaining very high recognition accuracy and low latency. Complex in-store scenes, frequent model updates, and the need for better small-file handling meant the company needed a faster data pipeline, stronger inference performance, and higher GPU utilization without turning platform operations into a bottleneck.
solution_summary: Lenztech and Alibaba Cloud upgraded the AI product-recognition platform behind Trax China's digital-shelf services with a layered cloud AI architecture. At the data-preparation tier, CPFS provides high-throughput, low-latency file storage so many workers can write images in parallel, while OSS keeps storage economics under control and lets image data move between cost and performance tiers. For inference, Lenztech connected its self-developed high-performance operator library to the DeepGPU toolkit, accelerating multiple computer-vision models so recognition jobs can hit both high-accuracy and low-latency targets. Around the serving layer, the team combined its existing containerized architecture with Alibaba Cloud's cloud-native AI suite so GPU sharing, memory isolation, and flexible scheduling policies can keep inference tasks stable even as model versions and workloads change quickly. The result is a faster, more economical vision platform for shelf and retail analytics.

solution_components.name: CPFS
solution_components.role: Provides the high-throughput parallel file layer for image preprocessing and small-file writes.

solution_components.name: Object Storage Service (OSS)
solution_components.role: Stores image assets economically and works with CPFS to balance cost and performance.

solution_components.name: DeepGPU
solution_components.role: Accelerates the inference of Lenztech's computer-vision models to meet accuracy and latency goals.

solution_components.name: Cloud-native AI suite
solution_components.role: Adds GPU sharing, memory isolation, and scheduling controls for the containerized inference platform.

data_flow: Retail images are written into CPFS and OSS, preprocessed for model input, and then sent to DeepGPU-accelerated computer-vision models on the cloud AI platform. The inference results are returned to retail analytics and shelf-monitoring services, while the cloud-native AI suite keeps GPU scheduling and model-serving resources stable as workloads and model versions evolve.
business_outcome: The Alibaba Cloud redesign helped Lenztech speed up the core vision pipeline behind its digital-shelf services. Data-processing time improved by more than 50%, DeepGPU accelerated vision inference by as much as 4.60x, GPU-cluster utilization improved 30%, and the platform kept 97%+ recognition accuracy while ensuring more than 95% of complex flows completed within 10 seconds.
metrics: small-file write latency above 100 ms fell below 5%
95%+ of complex flows finished within 10 seconds
architecture_clues: The storage design deliberately separates high-performance preprocessing on CPFS from lower-cost storage on OSS.
DeepGPU is combined with Lenztech's own operator library rather than used as a black-box inference layer.
The serving platform remains containerized and is enhanced with cloud-native AI scheduling controls for GPU sharing and memory isolation.
The platform is tuned for both high-frequency model iteration and large daily image volumes across many retail categories.
